item.title: A job that changed me: Working at a toy store was my teen feminist awakening
item.summary: I loved the business of selling toys – it felt like I was selling joy. But my least favourite part was the gendered language I was 15 when I landed my job at Toys R Us. Before that, my first job was a one-month stint at the local fish and chip shop, where I was paid in $20 bills slotted into Chiko roll packets. After a burn on my forearm (I still have it), I left the gig. That was the end of my hospitality career. This was 2014. I knew my strengths and weaknesses; I was no good with deep-fry baskets or carrying more than one thing in each hand. I wanted to work in the hallowed halls of retail. Continue reading...
